card: Omit response bodies when serving HTTP HEAD requests in the internal HTTP server, aligning with RFC 9110. Currently, the server outputs the body for HEAD responses, leaving stray bytes on persistent connections that can corrupt subsequent responses when operating behind connection-pooling reverse proxies like nginx. Unauthenticated clients can trigger this on both REST endpoints and the RPC 405 path. Functional tests are added to verify raw socket behavior.
evidence: PR description documents RFC 9110 section 9.3.2 non-compliance and shows reproduction: 'JSONRPC server handles only POST requests' body is emitted with a 405 Method Not Allowed header on HEAD requests.

PR description notes that because REST endpoints and the RPC 405 path answer HEAD without authentication, unauthenticated clients can trigger upstream keepalive connection desynchronization behind reverse proxies.
problem: HTTP HEAD responses currently transmit the full response body along with headers. Because compliant HTTP/1.1 clients stop reading at the end of the header section for HEAD requests, the unread body bytes remain on keep-alive connections, corrupting subsequent responses when proxied through connection-pooling reverse proxies like nginx.

risk.why: Flaws in HTTP connection handling could corrupt RPC or REST responses or cause connections to hang.

summary: Omit the response body when answering HTTP HEAD requests in the internal HTTP server. While the response headers, including Content-Length, continue to reflect what a GET request would return per RFC 9110, the server no longer writes the payload bytes over the wire. Functional tests are added to verify raw socket responses for both RPC and REST endpoints.
